extracted.intended_audience: researchers in NLP, medical informatics, and computational social science studying media coverage of health science research
extracted.subtask_description: Build interpretable statistical models to predict whether a published health science article will (1) receive a press release from the publishing journal and (2) garner mainstream media coverage, and to identify topical/content attributes that correlate with these outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: News values (proximity, significance, novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic 'news values' — defined as the elements of a story that make it likely to be published (examples: proximity, significance, novelty) — act as criteria for deciding what is newsworthy and most likely to increase audience attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use news-value concepts to reason about likely public interest in study findings; these are qualitative criteria used by journalists and PR practitioners when deciding what to pitch or issue as a press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release issuance as a target outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether journal editors issue a press release for an article (used here as a label for 'perceived newsworthiness' by journals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model this as a binary outcome (press release issued / not issued); the authors constructed PR datasets (Sumner PR, JAMA) and used matched negative sampling to control for venue/time. Predictive performance reported with AUC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mainstream media coverage as a target outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an article garners mainstream media coverage (used here as a label for actual news coverage received).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model this as a binary label (covered / not covered). The authors used Sumner NC and Reuters corpora with matched negative sampling and reported predictive performance with AUC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical/content features (unigrams and bigrams from titles and abstracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lexical features (counts of uni- and bigrams extracted from article titles and abstracts) used as primary predictors of press release issuance and media coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprocess with a standard English stop word list; keep features appearing in at least two instances; cap at most 50,000 most frequent features (dataset-specific caps reported). Rank predictive terms using bootstrap confidence intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: MeSH terms as features
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) drawn from the NLM controlled vocabulary and manually assigned to citations were included as features to capture topical/semantic content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat MeSH terms similarly to lexical features; MeSH prefixes (MH-/mh) appear in reported topic/feature lists and sLDA vocabularies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic-science topicality anticorrelates with newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Features indicative of basic science (examples given: 'binding', 'receptor', 'mice', 'protein') were observed to be negatively correlated with press release generation and media coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret negative predictive lists as evidence that mechanistic/basic-lab work is less likely to be considered newsworthy for lay audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population-level / epidemiological topicality correlates with newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics and words associated with population-level findings or common behaviors (examples given: 'women', 'pregnancy', 'alcohol', 'flu', '95% CI', 'cohort') correlated positively with press release issuance and media coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such topics likely map to perceived relevance/relatability for general audiences and thus increase probability of PR issuance or news coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matched negative sampling (same journal/issue/year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative instances (articles not receiving press releases or coverage) were sampled from the same journal and same issue (or same journal/year/volume) as positive instances to control for venue and temporal factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sumner PR: up to 10 negatives per positive (same journal/issue). Reuters: up to 20 negatives per positive (same journal/year/volume). This procedural requirement isolates content predictors from venue/time confounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminative modeling: L2-regularized logistic regression
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard logistic regression with a squared ℓ2 norm penalty as the discriminative classifier whose features are unigram/bigram and MeSH counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fit with LIBLINEAR; select regularization hyper-parameter λ via nested cross-validation (log line search from 1e-5 to 100). Report mean AUC over five-fold cross-validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance metric: area under the ROC curve (AUC)
rubrics_metrics.description: AUC is used as the main evaluation metric, reflecting the probability a positive instance ranks above a negative instance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute mean and SD across five-fold cross-validation; report fold ranges. Use AUC to compare model discriminative power across datasets/tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection and validation: five-fold nested cross-validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Five-fold cross-validation was used to estimate predictive performance; hyper-parameter selection (λ) performed via nested (tuned on training folds) cross-validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nested cross-validation when selecting hyper-parameters to avoid information leakage into test folds; report averaged metrics across folds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bootstrap confidence intervals for feature coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct bootstrap samples (1000 resamples) to estimate variance and approximate 95% confidence intervals around logistic regression coefficient estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rank robustly predictive features by the lower bound of their CI for positive predictors and by the upper bound for negative predictors. Use coefficient distributions from bootstrap to assess robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervised topic modeling (sLDA) to uncover discriminative topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use supervised latent Dirichlet allocation (sLDA) to uncover latent topics whose prevalences correlate with press release issuance or media coverage (labels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set number of topics K=20 (authors' chosen 'intuitively reasonable' value); set symmetric Dirichlet prior α=1; model document topic proportions and predict binary labels via a softmax; interpret topic coefficients to see positive/negative correlations with outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocabulary and feature-cap settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Vocabularies consisted of unique unigrams (from titles, abstracts, MeSH). Features were limited to the top-frequent words up to dataset-specific caps (examples: 50,000 features for several datasets; 10,004 for Sumner NC discriminative task; sLDA vocab sizes reported per corpus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep a reasonable cap to limit dimensionality; report the final number of features used for each dataset and modeling approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text preprocessing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard English stop word list applied; only keep features appearing in at least two instances in a dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply consistent preprocessing across datasets to ensure comparability; these choices affect feature sparsity and downstream model performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of press release text as alternative features for media prediction
rubrics_metrics.description: For predicting news coverage, consider using features extracted from the press release text as predictors (in addition to or instead of original article features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors found press-release-based models achieved somewhat different predictive performance; comparing models helps understand how press releases influence media uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation and reporting of top predictive n-grams and topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Report and interpret top positive and negative n-gram features and sLDA topics (top-N words per topic) and plot coefficient distributions to understand drivers of predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rank terms by CI bounds (bootstrap) rather than raw coefficients to emphasize robustness; visualize topic coefficients to convey which topics correlate with outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and caution about generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize limitations: inability to infer causality about why PRs were written or stories covered; news values vary across organizations; modeling focused on lexical/topic proxies and omitted higher-level study metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use caution when generalizing findings; consider adding higher-level features (cohort size, study design, basic vs applied) and richer linguistic features in future work to improve interpretability and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical implication: journals select press releases for relatable/lay-appropriate topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that scientific journals intentionally disseminate press releases that cover topics likely to be found 'newsworthy' by lay audiences (e.g., women, pregnancy, flu), which aids journalists and shapes public attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aiming for media uptake, consider emphasizing study aspects that increase general-audience relevance and ease of translation to lay language; but be mindful of potential selection biases.
